ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and record the driver's cancellation as fee-void; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning: The dispute enters the NS group through NS-0: the cancellation was made by the driver ([F4], cancelled_by = driver), so the fee's validity is tested under NS-1/NS-2 rather than the fixed-fare rules. The rider's complaint is that the fee was charged after a short wait ([F4], [F5], [F7]). Safety screening: I read all chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint ([F9], [F10], [F11], [F12]) — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern = none and no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation [SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS trace covers the whole wait with no hole, and even the arrival confirmation is a driver tap, not a platform auto-confirmation ([F1], [F2], [F3], [F5], [F6]) [NS-1]. NS-1 fails on its third element: NS-1 (i) and (ii) are met — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 and was 41 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m radius ([F6], [F1]) [NS-1] — but the driver then stayed within the radius only 1 min 40 s (100 s), short of the required more than 3 minutes before cancelling ([F6], [F2]) [NS-1]. His own chat "3 min up, cancelling the trip" ([F10]) does not match the record: the earliest approach was 14:13:25 ([F2]) and his tap 14:14:10 ([F6]), so cancelling at 14:15:50 ([F4]) cannot complete a 3-minute wait after arrival. Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not jointly satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is fully refunded to the rider [NS-2]. The NS-2 flag branch is not triggered — the trace settles that the arrival confirmation was made while the driver was within the radius ([F6], [F1]), so no false "I'm Here" and no account flag [NS-2]. The refund is payable as a Ryde voucher and Ryde retains final discretion ([F7]) [NS-7].
